text: Animalism, defended by Eric Olson and Peter van Inwagen, holds that:
choices: we are fundamentally human organisms, so our identity over time is the biological continuity of the same animal
we are bundles of perceptions with no underlying subject
we persist just in case our psychology is continuous, wherever it is realised
the self is a narrative construction that organises a life into a story
explanation: For the animalist you ARE the organism; you persist as long as that animal's life continues, even through severe psychological loss. Option 1 is Hume's bundle theory; option 2 is the psychological-continuity view animalism opposes; option 3 is the narrative account.
